title: [RFC] Drop Windows 7 support
body:
We all know it's coming and at least as far as i am concerned it was planned for v3. Now that we're rushing v3 for gtk4 i'm not sure sure anymore. I'll still put this into the v3 tracking board for now but we can move it into v4 later if we prefer.

For community members, please share your opinions! If you're fine with dropping Windows 7 support a 👍 reaction is enough, if you want/need Windows 7 support, we'd appreciate hearing more about your use-case (plus a 👎 reaction) :)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: gtk3-rs was unmaintained for 2 years and nobody cared. Now there's an Advisory for an old unsoundness issue (that seemingly never caused any problems in tauri) and everyone loses their shit. A fix in gtk3-rs seems to be unlikely so we'll accelerate the switch to gtk4, minimizing the breaking changes between tauri v2 and v3 so hopefully everyone updates quickly so we can kill v2 asap afterwards. (gtk4 was always planned for tauri v3, just not this quickly - the distro support should be roughly the same as webkitgtk4.1 in v2). For further questions, please move to one of those issues https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues?q=sort%3Aupdated-desc%20is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20gtk4 (trying my best to keep this one on-topic lol)

reporter
comments.body:
We use 1.77.2 in CI without major issues for example https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/.github/workflows/test-core.yml
Once a while i talk with app devs about this as well 🤷 

So far it was only one or two `cargo update` commands but if it's more for you'd i'd recommend to set your project's `rust-version` to 1.77.2 and use the new version aware resolver from cargo 1.84: https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/01/09/Rust-1.84.0.html#cargo-considers-rust-versions-for-dependency-version-selection which we use for tauri v1's CI which is still stuck on 1.60 / 1.61 https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/pull/12401/files

Edit: Just tried it without the new resolver:
0) `rustup default 1.77.2-msvc`
1) `pnpm create tauri-app`
2) `cd project/src-tauri`
3) `cargo update -p cargo_metadata --precise 0.19.0`
4) `cargo update -p cargo-platform --precise 0.1.8`
5) `pnpm tauri dev` (and other commands) works...

---

But yes, this is something we need to have in mind here as well, not only did Microsoft, Rust, WebView2 drop support for Windows 7, the crates are doing it as well so it will get harder and harder to maintain that MSRV.

comments.author: participant1
reporter
comments.body:
> What are the compromises to leave support for Windows 7?

Apart from requiring (maintenance) resources that we don't have? It forces us, or will force us, to hold back dependency updates (potentially some that fix CVEs etc) and having to keep compatibility with chromium/webview2 v109 (we're at 132 btw) also actively prevents us from implementing new features and fixing some bugs because not all things can be done in a backwards compatible way (for example switching the [hosting mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/concepts/windowed-vs-visual-hosting))

It's 2025 and i'm starting to believe that people who use or target windows 7 don't deserve access to the latest frameworks / framework versions, **especially one that has security as its number 1 priority.** At some point you just have to let it die or live with the consequences of not doing so.
But that's only _my_ opinion which is why this is an open issue and not just a decision we make behind the scenes.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
Here’s a use case for using Tauri on Windows 7: we have a task to rewrite an old application built in Delphi, and one of the main challenges is supporting the existing user base still running on outdated operating systems (about 10% of our users fall into this category).

There’s currently zero chance of dropping support for them, though we might be able to do so later (possibly in a few years) when this percentage decreases further.

We’d really love to choose Tauri now (because it’s fantastic). We’re willing to settle for older versions of the language/libraries and stick with them, as long as there’s still a possibility to build and run the application. In the future, even if delayed, we’d like to have the option to update.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> The current status is that Tauri (with the few plugins needed) does build and work with --target x86_64-win7-windows-msvc -Z build-std on "stable" 1.91.

That's very good to know because something i considered as well: Basically have Windows 7 be a tier 3 target for us just like it is for cargo. We wouldn't hold back our MSRV for it, probably test it even less (if that's even possible) perhaps without a guarantee that every minor release builds on release (since in theory some crates could break compat with the win7 rust target at any time). Maybeee we'd drop some special windows 7 things like the notification plugin's win7 feature flag etc idk

Since we're so short staffed at the moment i don't think we'd even do the _major_ changes that are currently blocked by Windows 7 support (eg Visual Hosting), other stuff can probably be put behind version checks quite easily.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I would also reference the follow discord conversation : https://discord.com/channels/616186924390023171/986184094050316358/1516804072253034596

the windows-rs crate subsystem now exclusively links a few COM apis against `combase.dll` instead of `ole32.dll` - (ref: https://github.com/microsoft/windows-rs/pull/3743)

The above means that specifically anything >= `windows 0.62.x`, `windows-sys 0.61.x` inherently won't work with Windows 7 pinning a few more dependencies at tauri's side because win7 target can't solve this exclusively.

A potentially solution may be a patch.crates-io but that can't be targetted downstream and hunting the libraries using the crates above as aforementioned is a harder task.

Technically, this forces an "official" drop of Windows 7. A potential guide on how to patch `windows`, `windows-rs` for tauri apps that need Windows 7 support is still plausible.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Sooo, looks like not many people here _actually_ cared about Windows 7 support since nobody noticed that the Webview2 installer wasn't working there for a while...
When you try to run the installer it will crash with `no entry point for GetPackagesByPackageFamily` (adding for searchability _if_ someone sees it on their machine after all)

With that last nail in the coffin we decided that Tauri version 2.11 is the last version to (semi-)officially support Windows 7 - though you have to get an old webview2 installer or fixed version somewhere yourself.
Starting in v2.12, Windows 7 support is no longer guaranteed and we will start to slowly raise our MSRV beyond 1.77 (the last rust version with built-in Windows 7 support - released March 2024!) as was planned when Tauri v2 was initially released.
That also opens up discussions about our MSRV policy, but this will happen in https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/15579 instead to not further pollute this issue. Please feel free to share your opinions about that over there :)

I know many people will be sad about this news and i apologize for that, but at some point we simply have to accept defeat.

Once we decided on a MSRV policy we will share a blog post on both topics, though there will be no news for avid readers of this issue.

P.S. If windows-rs someday re-adds windows 7 support, which i do not see happening, or if somebody wants to work on a guide with all the workarounds then we could talk about this topic again, eg to maybe add something that helps with getting an ancient installer version or something (assuming the old installer can still download the components...)
